title: Northforge Bio onramp scratch journal
content:
Call notes / scratch journal - Northforge Bio (initial technical intake)

Date: 2024-02-07 10:00 PT
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood), Liam O'Connor (Redwood Solutions), Dr. Priya Desai (Northforge CTO), Rashid Alami (Northforge SRE), Jordan Meyers (Data Ops)

High-level ask (customer paraphrase):
- Prototype an LLM assistant to help researchers surface protocol-relevant literature snippets and summarize experimental notes.
- Must run on customer-managed infra for next 6–9 months (data sensitivity + compliance).
- Low-latency interactive queries (sub-second to 1.5s target p95 for short queries).
- Cost-sensitive: want to understand tradeoffs between Dedicated vs Private deployment.

Notes / raw capture:
- Northforge handles genomic assay data and annotated lab notes; they cannot send raw PHI/identifiers off their network.
- Primary dataset: 120k lab notes (semi-structured), 30k internal protocols, 2M public literature abstracts for retrieval augmentation.
- Preferred network: initial PoC on VPC Private deployment (Redwood Private control plane, customer VPC peering), but they asked about a fully on-prem package if integration complexity high.
- Authentication: OkTA for staff, but want service-to-service auth via mTLS + internal KMS for model keys/HSM later.
- Audit/logging: must retain request/response audit for 365 days; need exportable logs for compliance team.
- Token budget: expect 1.8M tokens/day at PoC scale estimate (rough). Want ballpark cost for 100k queries/day scenario.

Functional requirements (as captured):
- Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with strict provenance: every generated claim must include a source link + confidence hint.
- Redaction / PII filter pre-send: must detect and redact any sample IDs, patient identifiers from requests and responses.
- Model determinism: for a subset of evaluation prompts they want stable responses (minimal drift) across model versions during evaluation window.
- Support for long context windows (up to ~16k tokens) for some protocol summarization use cases.
- Streaming response support desired for UI fluidity.

Non-functional / constraints:
- No egress of raw data (even embeddings) to third-party managed endpoints without explicit encryption and customer control.
- KMS/HSM integration required for key custody; ask about Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) flow for Private.
- On-prem GPU availability: they have 4x A100 nodes in a colo and may provision extra; but SRE unfamiliar with provisioning Base OS/runtime for Redwood Private.
- SLO: 99% of short queries <= 1.5s, 99% of long summarizations <= 6s.

Gotchas / open questions to resolve quickly:
- Embeddings privacy: can we perform local-only embedding computation with Redwood Private? (Yes, but need to map to packaging + infra ops doc).
- Data indexing cadence: they patch protocols weekly; how to support incremental re-index without full rebuild? Need guidance on incremental vector upserts and snapshotting.
- Encryption in transit inside colo: they insist on mTLS between Redwood runtime and their retrieval layer; need spec on cert rotation.
- Model selection: they want an initial curated medium-sized open model with 8k+ context; discuss quantization benefits vs accuracy regression. Need Redwood model recommendations and expected token-cost delta.
- Cost estimate cliff: customer expects rough monthly cost for 100k q/day; produce a simple breakdown (inference tokens + storage + infra) — ask pricing/finance for a draft.

Immediate action items (owners):
- Maya: send summary + initial architecture sketch (private-vpc vs onprem) and list of required infra ports and cert endpoints. Due: 2024-02-09.
- Liam: prepare recommended model shortlist with perf/cost tradeoffs (include quantized variants) and example latency numbers on A100. Due: 2024-02-12.
- Rashid (Northforge): share a sanitized sample of 200 lab-note snippets + schema for indexing (anonymized). Target: 2024-02-10.
- Jordan: dump of current search/index tech (Elasticsearch version + vector plugin?) and how they plan to serve retrieval. TBD.
- Solutions: schedule deep-dive with Redwood Private engineering to talk about BYOK + HSM integration. Propose slot: 2024-02-14 09:00 PT.

Risk notes (soft):
- If we push a smaller quantized model to meet cost SLO without validating on their scientific prompts, risk of hallucinations/incorrect citations. Need evaluation harness with their ground-truth prompts.
- SRE ramp: their infra team has limited experience with driver/kernel tuning for CUDA stacks; Redwood should provide an ops-runbook for driver versions + troubleshooting.

Evaluation / success criteria (customer):
- PoC can answer targeted protocol QA prompts with >= 85% precision on citation attribution (internal evaluation).
- Throughput: sustain 10 q/s peak on dev cluster without >5% latency SLO breaches.
- Compliance: logs + kms integration demoed and accepted by security lead.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Bring a short demo repo showing RAG + source citation (+ sample redaction hook) — fast win for first meeting.
- Create a short prompt set (30 prompts) mapped to gold citations for quick regression test.
- Check conformance of our audit export format with their SIEM (they use Splunk).

Next meeting: technical deep-dive (Redwood eng + Northforge SRE + data ops). Proposed agenda:
1) Infra: network, certs, S3/MinIO access patterns, ports
2) Model choice and quantization tradeoffs
3) Indexing: vector store, upserts, snapshotting cadence
4) Security: BYOK, HSM, audit retention export
5) Timeline and success metrics for 6-week PoC

End of scratch journal entry.

(If anything missing that we promised on call, update this file and ping collaborators)
